summary: Establish the universal exact-2n effective-switch theorem for every adjacent-gap maximizer and minimizer, together with its energy invariant, endpoint-count lemma, endpoint rigidity, discharged obligations, and solved research goal.

node.title: Saturated switching interfaces glue a global block-energy invariant
node.statement: For an arbitrary global adjacent-gap extremizer, the accepted finite bang-bang reduction and switch-zero condition imply a global block-energy difference K=-2(lambda_{n+1}-lambda_n), and hence strict endpoint derivative-magnitude inequalities.

node.title: Global energy invariant and strict endpoint slope dominance
node.statement: For every finite R>1, integer n>=2, and every global maximizer or minimizer rho_* of D_n on K_R, use DEF-NGE2-ENDPOINT-NORMING and any finite bang-bang representative. The blockwise quantity K=(u_n'^2+lambda_n rho_* u_n^2)-(u_{n+1}'^2+lambda_{n+1} rho_* u_{n+1}^2) glues across every effective switch to the global a.e. constant -2D_n(rho_*). Consequently q_0>1 and q_1<-1.

row.title: Universal exact-2n switching theorem for adjacent weighted Dirichlet gaps
row.headline_value: For every finite R>1 and n>=2, every global maximizer and minimizer has exactly 2n effective switches
row.scope: All measurable densities 1<=rho<=R a.e. on (0,1), every finite R>1, every integer n>=2, both global maxima and minima, and every extremizer
row.main_limitation: No symmetry, uniqueness, explicit switch locations, closed optimal-gap formula, infinite-contrast theorem, formal-proof-assistant verification, or novelty claim

rationale.quantifier_alignment: The proof fixes arbitrary finite R>1 and integer n>=2 and then treats every member of both global extremizer sets. It uses no selected branch, uniqueness, reflection symmetry, or contrast-asymptotic weakening.
rationale.proof_mechanism: Strict quotient monotonicity gives an exact endpoint-indicator formula for the switching-function zeros. Full one-sided saturation identifies simple zeros with effective switches. A block oscillator-energy difference has interface jump Delta rho times F, so it glues across every saturated switch and integrates to -2D. Endpoint traces then force q_0>1 and q_1<-1, activating both indicators.
rationale.independence: Three mechanism-distinct routes were frozen. Two analytic auditors independently reconstructed the energy invariant and exact-zero lemma, and a separate synthesis auditor returned PASS with no blocking, major, minor, or unresolved mathematical finding.
rationale.computation_policy: Finite topology scans and high-precision stationary calculations are bounded adversarial evidence only. They are not used for universal entailment or global-completeness certification.
rationale.novelty_policy: No novelty or priority claim is made. The primary-source search did not verify a theorem with the identical full scope, but inaccessible older literature prevents a priority conclusion.
rationale.scope_boundary: Symmetry, uniqueness, explicit switch locations, optimal-value formulae, infinite contrast, and transition laws remain outside the theorem.

ordered_steps: Fix an arbitrary global maximum or minimum and its accepted finite bang-bang representative.
On a constant-density block, differentiate each oscillator energy u_k'^2+lambda_k rho u_k^2 and obtain a constant.
At an effective interface use C1 matching and the accepted switch-zero condition to compute the sole jump as Delta rho times F and make it vanish.
Integrate the glued constant over the unit interval; kinetic and weighted normalization each contribute lambda_n-lambda_{n+1}, giving K=-2D.
Read K at the Dirichlet endpoints and use the fixed left orientation and Sturm parity to obtain q_0>1 and q_1<-1.
boundary_cases: A.e. density representatives use essential block values and common one-sided eigenfunction traces.
Maximum and minimum switch directions differ but the zero jump is direction independent.
The strict inequalities hold for every fixed finite R>1, including R near one and arbitrarily large finite R.

ordered_steps: Orient consecutive eigenfunctions and prove W=u_{n+1}'u_n-u_{n+1}u_n'<0 throughout the open interval from strict interlacing and W'=-(lambda_{n+1}-lambda_n)rho u_nu_{n+1}.
Conclude that Q=u_{n+1}/u_n is strictly decreasing on each u_n nodal interval and list its exact first, middle, and last one-sided limits.
Rewrite F=lambda_{n+1}u_n^2(c^2-Q^2) and count the two levels Q=+c and Q=-c, with strict endpoint indicators and no contribution from equality.
Differentiate at every crossing to prove all zeros are simple.
Use the reproduced Feynman-Hellmann formula and localized one-sided box variations to prove complete max/min saturation, so every simple zero and only every simple zero is an effective switch.
boundary_cases: For n=2 there are no middle nodal cells and the formula still has the correct four possible contributions.
The cases q_0=c and q_1=-c add no interior zero.
No quotient is used across a pole, and fixed endpoints are not counted as switches.
external_results: The accepted upstream CLM-NGE2-ZERO-BOUND is in the same measurable Sturm-Liouville scope; the current proof package independently reproduces the strict Wronskian and level-crossing argument needed for the stronger exact count.

Both indicators equal one, so the effective switch count is 2n.
